hypotheses.construction_plan: Introduce an undefined bivariate function K(x,y). Instantiate x=n,y=m to obtain K(n,m); instantiate x=n,y=n to obtain K(n,n), the diagonal specialization. The Piecewise expression is the guard-selected evaluation of these two instances under Ne(n,m).
required_assumptions: K is an undefined function of two positional arguments
n and m are scalar symbols
the Piecewise condition Ne(n,m) distinguishes the off-diagonal instance from the diagonal instance
proof_obligations: K(n,m) - K(x,y) under the substitution x=n,y=m = 0
K(n,n) - K(x,y) under the substitution x=n,y=n = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The two non-identical subexpressions are calls to the same undefined binary function K. K(n,n) is the diagonal specialization of K(x,y), while K(n,m) is the full off-diagonal instance. This explains the shared function family and the branch dependency without assuming a physical interpretation.
